factorPolicy.handling: Use provider raw hourly UV values as the forecast signal; do not apply an additional cloud or shade multiplier.
Use actual overlap with each hourly forecast bin, including partial first and last hours.
Calculate durations only over covered intervals, break continuity across gaps, and disclose missing periods.

Temperature and precipitation remain display context. Cloud cover may add a conditional explanation when very cloudy hours overlap with elevated forecast UVI; it never changes UV values, durations, or protection thresholds.
May explain whether an outing overlaps daylight or twilight; darkness is not a health-risk adjustment.
Give general shade advice, but do not infer route shade or apply a numeric shade reduction.
Offer complementary general protection actions; do not infer what the person wears or calculate covered-skin protection.
When covered UVI reaches 3, mention conditionally that snow, bright sand, or water can add reflected UV; do not infer the surface or apply a numeric multiplier.
Make sunscreen reminders conditional; do not assume use, application time, amount, or product label.
When covered UVI reaches 3, include conditional reapplication advice after swimming, sweating, or towel drying; do not infer the activity or calculate a timer.
Do not collect, infer, or quantify personal vulnerability, skin sensitivity, or medicine-related photosensitivity; this is not an individualized medical model.

sourceBackedConcepts: WHO says higher UV Index means greater potential for skin and eye harm and less time before harm can occur.
WHO recommends sun protection from UV Index 3 and describes clothing, shade, eye protection, and sunscreen for uncovered skin.
WHO describes sunscreen reapplication every two hours, particularly after sweating, swimming, playing, or outdoor exercise.
WHO notes that clouds do not always block UV and that snow, sand, and water can reflect UV.
uvScoutProductChoices: Use raw UVI bands below 3, 3 to below 8, and 8 or higher to describe the forecast profile.
Always give a practical outcome for covered UV below 3, without treating daytime and nighttime differently.
When covered UVI reaches 3, show clothing, shade, eye protection, and sunscreen advice for the relevant hours; highlight UVI 8+ periods for extra shade.

Show the extra two-hour reapplication reminder only when at least 7200 covered seconds are forecast at UVI 3 or higher; this display trigger is a UV Scout product choice, not a WHO rule or a personal timer.
Keep WHO's general action table in Info; place UV Scout actions before a short profile summary in the outing result.
